answer: In PoA, trust propagates as a bounded-length random walk on the attestation graph: each step diffuses endorsement mass, while normalization limits any node’s influence. A Sybil cluster typically connects to honest nodes through a sparse external cut, yielding low conductance. Cheeger-style bounds then limit walk mass—and therefore aggregate voting weight—inside the cluster, even when its identities share a cipher, wharf, or pigment as labels.
